design_summary.purpose: Adaptive active-aerodynamics controller shell that supervises an external surrogate service through bounded request/response transport, validates returned compact commands, enforces safety limits, and provides deterministic fallback behavior for FPGA implementation.
design_summary.operating_model: The top-level RTL operates as a safety-critical transport-and-supervision FSM with IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and TIMEOUT behavior. It captures compact configuration through a 64-bit register window, issues one bounded 128-bit request per transaction, tracks request_tag and freshness/timeout context, validates the response contract before command acceptance, clamps final actuator commands to configured bounds, and transitions to deterministic fallback on malformed, stale, late, or invalid responses. The RTL is agnostic to physics internals and only handles compact command-relevant metadata and handshakes around an external GPU or remote service.

external_interfaces.name: cfg_window
external_interfaces.intent: Compact configuration and status access for mode enable, watchdog limit, freshness limit, clamp bounds, geometry descriptor ID, control profile selection, and hold-last-good policy.

external_interfaces.name: model_request_stream
external_interfaces.intent: Emit bounded request packets containing request_tag, geometry descriptor ID, stream velocity summary, profile selection, and health/status bits.

external_interfaces.name: model_response_stream
external_interfaces.intent: Receive compact response packets from the external surrogate service for validation and command extraction.

external_interfaces.name: actuator_command_stream
external_interfaces.intent: Deliver validated, clamped, or deterministic fallback actuator commands only after safety checks.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Synthesizable top-level supervisory controller for the external aerodynamic surrogate workflow.
responsibilities: Capture and retain compact configuration fields from the 64-bit window: mode enable, watchdog limit, freshness limit, command min/max clamp bounds, geometry descriptor ID, control profile selection, and hold-last-good policy.
Implement the top-level safety FSM with IDLE, ISSUE_REQUEST, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, APPLY_COMMAND, FALLBACK, and TIMEOUT states.
Coordinate request issuance, response acceptance, timeout supervision, stale-data detection, validation gating, fallback entry, and actuator command presentation.
Maintain request_tag tracking and outstanding-transaction context so stale, duplicated, or out-of-order responses can be rejected.
Expose status bits for busy, request_pending, response_valid, stale_detected, timeout_detected, clamp_applied, fallback_active, and fault_latched.
Reset to a safe fallback condition with outputs deasserted or conservative defaults.
interface_notes: Uses only compact interfaces: 64-bit register window, 128-bit request/response streams, and 32-bit actuator command stream.
Must not expose wide geometry, mesh, pressure, flow-field, or tensor ports.
Must ensure top-level outputs are driven by real RTL drivers and not only connected to child inputs.
External model transport follows the mandatory direction contract: req_valid/req_data are outputs, req_ready is input, rsp_valid/rsp_data are inputs, rsp_ready is output.
ownership_notes: Owns top-level control, status, and transaction supervision.
Owns register-window decode and readback packaging.
Owns inter-module fanout of configuration and supervisory status.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_request_packer
module_architecture.role: Internal bounded request formatter for external surrogate transport.
responsibilities: Compose compact request packets within 128 bits.
Package request_tag, geometry_descriptor_id, stream_velocity_mps, profile selector, and health/status bits into the request record.
Emit request_issued_pulse when a request event is accepted and the packet is launched.
Hold req_valid until the request handshake completes according to req_ready.
Avoid any inference of solver behavior or large payload buffering.
interface_notes: Consumes only compact metadata inputs and emits the bounded request stream.
Does not drive upstream configuration or external ready signals.
Keeps payload-related metadata fixed-width and FPGA-synthesizable.
ownership_notes: Owns the request packet formatting contract and request_tag export to the supervisor.
Owns the outbound request data path only; no geometry or tensor storage is implied.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_response_guard
module_architecture.role: Internal validator, stale-data detector, and watchdog manager for external responses.
responsibilities: Check exact request_tag match against the outstanding transaction context.
Compare request age against freshness_limit and watchdog_limit.
Reject stale, duplicated, out-of-order, malformed, or late packets.
Assert stale_detected, timeout_detected, and fault_detected as appropriate.
Expose validated_request_tag and a compact validated_command only after acceptance.
Drive rsp_ready according to supervisory consumption policy.
interface_notes: Receives the external response stream using the mandatory direction contract.
Outputs only compact, bounded command-relevant data and detection flags.
Does not expose surrogate tensors or model internals.
ownership_notes: Owns response acceptance logic and timeout/freshness enforcement.
Owns the validated command candidate handed to the safety stage.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety_fallback
module_architecture.role: Internal safety, clamp, and fallback command generator.
responsibilities: Clamp accepted commands to configured min/max bounds before any actuator presentation.
Generate a deterministic conservative fallback command when faults occur or when response validation fails.
Support hold-last-good behavior only when explicitly configured.
Assert act_cmd_valid only when the command has passed validation and clamping, or when a deterministic fallback command is intentionally asserted.
Expose clamp_applied, fallback_active, act_cmd_valid, act_cmd_data, and last_good_command_out.
interface_notes: Consumes validated_command and fault_latched from the supervisory flow.
Produces the final actuator command stream within 32 bits.
Must prevent out-of-range commands from propagating to the actuator output.
ownership_notes: Owns final command selection between validated, held, and fallback values.
Owns final safety gating before act_cmd_valid assertion.

interface_summary.intent: Top-level configuration and supervision metadata are forwarded to the request packer, which turns a request event into a bounded 128-bit request packet and request issuance pulse.
The request packer emits the outbound request stream, exports the request_tag used for transaction tracking, and provides the issuance indication consumed by the top-level FSM.
The top-level and supervisory context supply the response guard with the external response stream and the outstanding transaction limits needed for validation.
The response guard indicates acceptance or rejection status, timeout/stale conditions, and handshake readiness back to the top-level supervisor.
A validated compact command candidate is passed to the safety stage, which then decides whether to clamp, apply, hold, or replace it with fallback behavior.
The top-level configuration and external actuator handshake control the final command bounding and optional hold-last-good policy.
The safety stage publishes the final actuator command, clamp and fallback indicators, and the last-known-good command state used by the supervisory layer.

data_flow_summary: A configuration write into the 64-bit window captures the compact mode and safety parameters, including enable, watchdog and freshness limits, clamp bounds, geometry descriptor ID, profile selector, and hold-last-good policy.
A request_event causes the top-level to coordinate request issuance through adaptive_aero_control_request_packer, which increments or manages request_tag and emits a bounded 128-bit request packet.

The external service returns a response on the 128-bit response stream; adaptive_aero_control_response_guard checks tag match, freshness, malformed conditions, and watchdog expiry before exposing a validated_command.
If the response is valid, the safety stage clamps the command to configured bounds and only then asserts act_cmd_valid to the actuator stream.
If the response is invalid, stale, duplicate, out-of-order, malformed, late, or times out, the supervisor latches fault and transitions into FALLBACK or TIMEOUT as applicable.
In FALLBACK, adaptive_aero_control_safety_fallback emits a deterministic conservative command, optionally retaining the last known good command only when explicitly configured.
Status outputs are updated to reflect busy, pending request, response validity, stale detection, timeout, clamp application, fallback activity, and fault latch state.
The architecture remains decoupled from the physics model internals, allowing a future GPU-service adapter to be added without changing the safety contract or top-level interface shape.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single synchronous clock domain is used for the top-level controller and all internal modules, with clk distributed to the request packer, response guard, and safety/fallback stage.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is an active-low reset input used synchronously across safety-critical state. Reset initializes the FSM to IDLE, clears outstanding transaction context, deasserts request/response/actuator valid signals, clears stale/timeout/fault/clamp/fallback indicators, and places the actuator command in a conservative safe fallback default.

integration_notes: The top-level transport direction contract is mandatory: model-request valid/data are outputs and model-request ready is an input; model-response valid/data are inputs and model-response ready is an output.
The architecture uses compact fixed-width metadata only and intentionally avoids wide geometric, mesh, pressure-field, flow-field, or surrogate-tensor pins.
All payload-related metadata is bounded and fixed-width, and any future bulk history or payload storage should map through technology-neutral BRAM abstraction rather than flattened registers.
The FPGA implementation path must not instantiate Sky130 hard macros; any future ASIC path would require separate collateral-gated memory handling.
The design must not deadlock; when the external service is unavailable or late, the FSM must recover to IDLE or FALLBACK and allow new requests after fault handling.
Command clamping must prevent out-of-range values from reaching act_cmd_data, and act_cmd_valid must only assert after validation and clamping or deliberate deterministic fallback.
Host firmware or software remains responsible for invoking the external DoMINO service on GPU or remote NIM using the same request semantics as the RTL transport layer.
Verification should include assertions that stale packets are rejected, timeout transitions force fallback, and clamp limits are enforced.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
The output preserves the specified module responsibilities and explicit inter-module interface contracts without redefining or renaming them.
